answer: In node2vec, the binary operator g(u,v) is not defined from the graph edge set itself; it is a function that combines the learned embeddings of two nodes u and v to produce an edge-level feature vector. If the implementation or description says it “relies on an edge existing,” that means the pair (u,v) is only treated as a candidate edge/example when there is an actual edge in the graph (for positive training examples or edge prediction). The operator then forms g(u,v) by applying a fixed combination rule to the two node vectors, such as concatenation, elementwise average, Hadamard product, or absolute difference. So the existence of an edge is used to decide which node pair to evaluate, but the binary operator itself does not require the edge to compute the combined vector once the two node embeddings are available.
confidence_reasoning: This is consistent with the standard node2vec edge-feature construction, though wording about “relying on an edge existing” can vary by source and task setup.
